briefings.title: Inside the Urgent Effort to Prepare America’s Workforce for a Massive AI Disruption
briefings.tldr: Former U.S. Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo leads the new organization RAISE US to prevent severe economic and gender inequality from AI disruption by partnering with state governors and business leaders on career transition pilots.

briefings.title: Gina Raimondo: Why rival AI giants are funding her $500M worker plan | Rapid Response
briefings.tldr: Former U.S. Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo has launched "Raise US," a $500 million bipartisan initiative backed by rival tech giants to fund state-level pilot programs and reform workforce policies, preparing American workers for AI-fueled job displacement.

briefings.title: Coffee with Crow: Building A Future Where Everyone Can Work with AI | ASU+GSV Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: To prevent a repeat of the "China shock" displacement of the 1980s, the U.S. must establish a "grand bargain" where employers and universities co-design a continuous, "K to grey" learning system that prioritizes individual empowerment over shareholder-only gains.

briefings.title: Odd Lots Gina Raimondo v003
briefings.tldr: To win the global AI race against China, the U.S. must prioritize strategic alliances and create a robust domestic "transition system" to manage massive labor displacement, as industrial policy alone cannot achieve total self-sufficiency.

briefings.title: Gina Raimondo on How European Industry Is Getting Crushed | Odd Lots
briefings.tldr: Former Commerce Secretary Gina Raimondo argues that the U.S. must prioritize bipartisan industrial policy and international alliances to win the AI and semiconductor race against China, warning that failing to create a "transition system" for displaced workers could lead to mass unemployment and the collapse of democratic stability.
